issue_summary.TYPE_CHECK: Biological replicate indices, the right field.
issue_summary.SOURCE_CHECK: The paper describes a gold standard spike-in sample set consisting of five samples, each measured in triplicates.
issue_summary.TRUTH_CHECK: The runs are grouped by source (Sample 1 to 5). Each sample is a single biological unit (a specific spike-in state). Therefore, all three runs for Sample 1 should share an index, all three for Sample 2 should share an index, and so on. However, independent biological units of one condition (or in this case, different states of the same gold standard set) must be distinguished by different indices if they are independent units. But the definition states "Independent biological units of one condition get 1, 2, 3". Here, the "condition" is the spike-in state. Since there are 5 different states, and each state is a single biological preparation measured 3 times, each state is its own biological unit. The runs for Sample 1 are technical replicates (index 1), Sample 2 are technical replicates of a different biological unit (index 2), etc. Assigning "1" to all 15 runs across 5 different samples is incorrect.
issue_summary.COMPLETENESS_CHECK: Every run is assigned a value.
